anomaly_def.Name: Transaction Lock Contention Anomaly + Data Block and Index Integrity Anomaly + Network and Connectivity Resource Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Transaction Lock Contention Anomaly : Concurrent sessions request incompatible locks on the same rows, pages, or metadata, forming long blocking chains or deadlocks that stall commit progress.
Data Block and Index Integrity Anomaly : On-disk pages or index structures are physically or logically corrupt, making navigation paths unreliable and forcing the engine to surface corruption errors or fall back to expensive full scans.
Network and Connectivity Resource Anomaly : Client-server communication or listener capacity is saturated or unstable, lengthening connect, read, or write operations and exhausting backend connection slots.

When all three faults coexist, the database exhibits a blended failure pattern: transactions obtain locks and then linger because corrupted pages or forced full-table rescans slow I/O, while simultaneous network slowdowns stretch round-trip times and postpone lock release. Blocker–waiter chains grow rapidly, deadlock detector activity spikes, and corruption-induced retries or failed statements multiply the number of sessions competing for locks and connections. Clients observe erratic response times, intermittent corruption or deadlock errors, authentication or connection-timeout failures, and dramatic drops in throughput as both in-engine and network wait events dominate performance dashboards.

Causally, page or index corruption degrades access paths, inflating I/O latency and statement duration; these long-running statements hold locks longer, heightening the likelihood of contention and deadlocks. Prolonged lock waits keep transactions open, increasing the population of active connections just as network bottlenecks restrict new session establishment and slow result streaming. Network stalls further delay commits and rollbacks, extending lock lifetimes and compounding contention. The ensuing retries and connection churn feed back into the network layer, while repeated scans of corrupt structures exacerbate I/O and CPU load, creating a self-reinforcing loop that destabilizes both concurrency control and connectivity handling, potentially cascading into widespread application timeouts and availability loss.

entry.official_definition: The number of seconds to wait for a block to be written to a connection before aborting the write.
entry.trigger_condition: The server waits longer than net_write_timeout while writing a block to the client connection.
entry.default_behavior: Defined as a MySQL server system variable.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when a statement cannot obtain the required lock within the configured waiting window because another transaction or metadata operation is holding an incompatible lock.
entry.solution_guidance: Inspect blocking sessions, reduce conflicting transaction overlap, shorten transaction lifetime, and review lock scheduling and schema-change timing.
